title: Himanta Returns: Assam CM Sworn In for Second Term May 12
excerpt: Governor formally appoints Sarma under Article 164 after BJP-led NDA wins a commanding 102 of 126 assembly seats.
body:
Himanta Biswa Sarma takes the oath of office as Chief Minister of Assam on Tuesday, May 12 — beginning his second consecutive term atop one of India's most strategically significant northeastern states.

**What Happened:**
Governor Lakshman Prasad Acharya formally appointed Sarma following the BJP's landslide victory, issuing an official notification through the Parliamentary Affairs Department under Article 164(1) of the Constitution of India. The swearing-in ceremony takes place at 11:40 AM at Veterinary College Field, Khanapara, Guwahati. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend as chief guest.

**Why the Mandate Matters:**
The BJP-led NDA won 102 of 126 assembly seats, securing a commanding two-thirds majority — and the BJP secured a majority on its own in Assam for the first time. At the BJP Legislature Party meeting in Guwahati, eight BJP MLAs proposed Sarma's name, the proposal was seconded by all other MLAs present, and he was then unanimously accepted as NDA leader in a joint meeting with AGP and BPF legislators. More than 50,000 people are expected to gather at the venue, making it one of the biggest political events in Assam in recent years.

**What to Watch:**
The final cabinet composition is expected to balance regional representation, community equations, and administrative experience — with the Assam cabinet permitted a maximum of 18 ministers besides the Chief Minister. Sources indicate the cabinet is likely to see further expansion at a later stage, with several BJP legislators still being considered for ministerial berths.
nri_angle: For Indian-Americans with roots in Assam and the Northeast, Sarma's second term signals policy continuity on infrastructure, identity politics, and the region's economic integration — issues that directly shape prospects for families still based there.
author: Diaspora Desk
